**Monsters look solid in the light.** Each sprite's outline is now turned
into a rounded body when it loads: the torso a broad cylinder, arms, legs and
guns thinner ones of their own. Lights near you shade a monster like a figure
standing in the room rather than a flat cardboard cutout.

**A flashlight you carry.** The beam now sits at your right shoulder, a
little behind your eyes like Doom 3's. It lights the floor ahead from above,
sways gently with your weapon as you walk, and no longer hides inside walls
you hug. Where it lands, it bounces a soft light in the color of what it
hits, so a lit wall spills onto the dark floor in front of it.

**Light that reads on dark colors.** Flashlight, muzzle flashes and fireballs
now brighten saturated colors toward their own hue, the way the palette's
ramps do, so dark blue carpet and deep red stone show the beam instead of
swallowing it. Bright walls in the beam no longer jump far ahead of the dark
floor beside them.

**More windows.** Windows set deep into walls now get glass too: the side
windows of E1M2's big room, deep windows in E1M5, viewing slots in E2M5,
E3M4 and E4M7, and one each in MAP15 and MAP29. DOOM now finds 101
windows, DOOM II 79.

**Reflections face the right way.** You and the monsters in window
reflections were mirrored back to front: turn left and your reflection looked
right. They now turn as a real mirror shows them.
